# temps_project_dsn (Resource)

A DSN a Sentry SDK reports a project's errors to, optionally tied to one environment. Destroying the resource revokes it; changing it creates a new DSN.

Import with `<project_id>/<id>`.

Required API key permissions: `error_tracking:read`, `error_tracking:create`, `error_tracking:write`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "temps_project_dsn" "frontend" {
  project_id     = temps_project.web.id
  name           = "frontend"
  environment_id = data.temps_environment.production.id
}

output "frontend_dsn" {
  value     = temps_project_dsn.frontend.dsn
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `project_id` (Number) ID of the project.

### Optional

- `base_url` (String) Public URL the DSN points at; the instance URL when unset. Temps never returns it, so changes made outside Terraform are not detected.
- `environment_id` (Number) Environment the events are filed under.
- `name` (String) Name of the DSN.

### Read-Only

- `dsn` (String) The DSN to configure in the SDK.
- `id` (String) Import ID, `<project_id>/<id>`.
- `public_key` (String) Public key part of the DSN.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <project_id>/<id>
terraform import temps_project_dsn.frontend 8/3
```
